items.title: fix(doctor): check sandboxes the runtime enables per agent (#207213)
items.summary: fix(doctor): check sandboxes the runtime enables per agent (#207213) ## Problem `openclaw doctor` and `doctor --fix` decided whether sandboxing is on from `agents.defaults.sandbox` only (#201988). With sandboxing enabled only per agent (`agents.entries..sandbox.mode`), Doctor gave no Docker/Podman warning and built no missing image. The first sign of trouble was a failed sandboxed turn. The runtime resolves each agent's sandbox with `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`. ## Change Doctor now resolves the defaults and every configured agent through `resolveSandboxConfigForAgent`, the runtime's own resolver. This is the same pattern as #205395. - An agent's own `sandbox.mode`, backend and images count. A gateway role that requires a sandbox covers every agent's resolved images. - Each container engine is probed once, and each distinct image is checked and offered for build once. - When the engine is missing, the note names the agent whose mode enabled it ("set sandbox.mode to off for agent \"work\""). An enabled mode is named before a role-only requirement. - Sandbox settings the runtime resolver rejects (for example a relative SSH workspace root) are reported as a Doctor warning instead of failing the step. ## User impact Doctor and the runtime now agree on which sandboxes exist. Users with per-agent sandboxing get the Docker/image warning and the build offer they were missing. ## Evidence - Red on main, green here: `doctor-sandbox.warns-sandbox-enabled-without-docker.test.ts` "follows an agent's own sandbox mode when the defaults leave it off (#201988)": the engine note and pending image work. - Adversarial review (Fable) found four gaps in round 1, all fixed and tested here: a role requirement hid an enabled agent; duplicate prompts per image; a throw on an invalid SSH root; role-required agents' own images. - `doctor-sandbox*.test.ts` 32/32; `tsgo:core` clean. - Not in scope, pre-existing: the Codex bwrap network-namespace hint still reads the defaults' `docker.network`. - Upgrade check from the latest stable: `openclaw@2026.11.10` wrote the state, and the config was given `agents.entries.work.sandbox: { mode: "all", docker: { image: "openclaw-sandbox:w11-missing" } }`. - `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` on 2026.11.10: no sandbox image finding. - This branch on the same state: `Sandbox base image missing: openclaw-sandbox:w11-missing`. - Lint fix after CI: the engine field uses the named `SandboxContainerEngine` type. Local ClawSweeper on `90fc97dc`: clean. Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi

items.title: fix: tell the user when a finished subagent's report can't start in t…
items.summary: fix: tell the user when a finished subagent's report can't start in their chat (#207194) ## What Problem This Solves When a subagent finishes, OpenClaw runs a turn in the parent chat to report the result. If that turn fails before it starts (for example, the chat's access program is not available for the model), the user in the channel sees nothing. The completion ends undelivered with only a log warning. ## User Impact When a channel-delivered subagent report turn (settle or announce) fails before it starts, the user now gets one failure notice in that channel: "OpenClaw couldn't finish this request…". This is the notice requester turns already get when model-runtime admission refuses them (#171021), which keeps working for every delivered turn. A direct-message completion that owes the user a reply instead receives the child's result as plain text. Unchanged: ordinary chat turns keep their own failure surfaces for other errors; a turn that started and then failed gets no notice and no resend, because its reply may already have reached the user; private and internal runs, cancelled runs and revoked sources stay silent. ## Why This Change Was Made The command runner (`run-embedded-attempt.ts`) owns the channel-visible failure notice for a turn that never started. #171021 qualified it only for a typed initial admission refusal (a wrapper class plus a first-candidate check), so it could prove the turn had committed no work. The runner already tracks that fact per run: `executionStarted` is set by the runtime's lifecycle `start`, and the runner already reports `providerStarted: false` on its lifecycle error when it is false. The qualifier is now `!executionStarted` plus either a subagent completion turn (any pre-start failure, on any fallback candidate) or a runtime admission refusal (any delivered turn, as before). A live model switch still retries. The `PreparedModelRuntimeInitialRunAdmissionError` wrapper and the candidate counter existed only for the old qualifier, so they are removed. Direct-message completions run with `deliver: false`, so no command notice reaches them. For those, the rethrown error carries `providerStarted: false`, and `resolveFailedAnnounceResponse` takes its existing text fallback on that fact. It now reads a structural `incomplete_result` code instead of matching a message regex. The cases do not overlap: with `deliver: true` the command returns a failed result, so the announce error path is not reached. Not changed, on purpose: - No transcript-only notice (`recordGatewaySessionRunFailure` or chat inject): those never reach channel users. - No resend on "any failure without send evidence". Message-tool send evidence exists only on successful results, so that rule would duplicate replies the model already sent by tool. Known gaps, named but not coded: - Gateway shutdown aborts every run with one shared reason object, so the mark is skipped when the run's abort signal has fired. - The notice copy is generic. Billing and rate-limit specific copy (`resolveAgentRunFailureNotice`) does not apply to this path, as before. - The WebSocket `callGateway` path loses the error cause, so there an incomplete model response no longer triggers text. Completions dispatch in-process. - A custom CLI backend that sends through loopback message delivery without streaming tool starts could still get a duplicate. Bundled backends stream tool starts. ## Evidence - End to end, real Gateway and qa-channel (QA Lab, mock provider; the failure happens before any provider call). A parent in a direct chat spawns a subagent. The parent is then switched to a provider whose API key is a missing secret, so its report turn fails before dispatch with `SecretSurfaceUnavailableError`. - Merge base `7e7e84039907`: the completion turn fails and "Subagent completion direct announce failed" is logged. The chat shows only the parent's "Worker started."; the child's result never arrives. - This branch at `7ec8889d61`: the chat shows "Worker started." and then the child's result text exactly once, through one direct-fallback receipt. The parent made 0 provider requests after the switch. - The scenario is not committed here; it can follow as a regression scenario. - In-process run against the real access gate (throwaway test): the `agent` dispatch rejected with `GatewayClientRequestError` → cause `FailoverError(OPENAI_ACCESS_PROGRAM_UNAVAILABLE, providerStarted: false)`, with 0 provider requests. - `agent-command.admission-failure.test.ts`: on a completion turn, an ordinary error, a missing runtime owner and a refusal after a live model switch each deliver one channel notice; a runtime refusal of an ordinary chat turn still does. Private, internal, cancelled, revoked-source, started-execution runs and an ordinary chat error deliver nothing. Owner mark: set before start, absent after start. The existing sent and failed delivery receipts still pass. - `subagent-announce-obligation.test.ts`: a pre-start failure and an incomplete model response choose the text fallback. A turn that started and then failed does not. - The new tests fail on the merge base and pass here; every silent case passes on both. - Not run end to end: the group-chat notice path (covered by the command tests above). Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi
